name: Lightpanda Cloud

modes.label: Cloud headless browser
modes.note: Builder overage; Explorer has hard 10 hour monthly quota. Browser not Chromium; no pixel-perfect GUI guarantee. Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee. Cloud serves the Lightpanda engine by default; browser=chrome runs Google Chrome for debugging only ('Chrome isn't intended for production traffic'). Metered by the second; concurrency overflow returns HTTP 429.

plans.name: Explorer
plans.note: 10 hours/month; BYOP; do not price unlimited usage at free tier.

plans.name: Builder
plans.note: 300 hours×$.08=$24 overage-equivalent included value; then $.08/hour. BYOP.

features.ip_note: Default fast_dc (single shared datacenter IP) or rotating shared datacenter pool with country; no residential offered, BYO proxy via console (Explorer and Builder).

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Resource-footprint and performance marketing comparisons are not CPU/RAM allocation guarantees. Compatibility is a CDP/WebAPI subset, not full Chrome desktop.
Builder concurrency 30 cannot fulfill 50 simultaneous browsers without Enterprise. Card preserves unknown resources null.

Cloud docs: metered by the second. CDP connection closes after 15 minutes regardless of quota; MCP idle timeout 5 minutes, active sessions can continue. Channel-specific cap cannot be represented by one max_session_h.

No graphics rendering pipeline: screenshot CDP returns a placeholder, not actual rendered page pixels. Local PNG/PDF output is text-only per README. This is not a screenshot-driven computer-use desktop substitute.

fleet.notes: Rendered pricing confirms 5/30. Browser sessions rather than generic VMs. 10 fits Builder; 50/300/1,000 need custom terms.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A CDP connection closes after 15 minutes, whatever your pool has left, so split long jobs across sessions.
snapshot_auto.note: Sessions are ephemeral browser sessions; no state save/restore documented. Hosted headless browser reached only over token-authenticated CDP / MCP (SSE) / HTTP fetch API; the customer gets no machine, shell, disk or exposed ports.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: CDP server ( serve ) Yes Yes MCP server Yes, all tools Partial, subset of tools AI agent Yes No fetch command Yes No HTTP API No Yes
snapshot_on_demand.note: Cloud interfaces are CDP, partial MCP and HTTP fetch only; no snapshot/checkpoint API. Cookies/storage live per session only.

harness_api.note: Feature-coverage table: built-in Lightpanda AI agent is Local=Yes, Cloud=No. Cloud MCP server (SSE) lets an external agent use the browser as a tool, which is not a harness API.

ingress_rules.quote: Lightpanda Cloud runs the browser for you. With no process to install or keep alive, an API token is all you need to drive it over CDP, MCP, or the HTTP API.
ingress_rules.note: Not applicable: no user-exposed ports/URLs; the only way in is the token-authenticated CDP/MCP/API endpoint.

guest_firewall.note: No shell/root in a hosted browser session; nothing to run nftables in. Hosted headless browser reached only over token-authenticated CDP / MCP (SSE) / HTTP fetch API; the customer gets no machine, shell, disk or exposed ports.

secret_proxy.quote: Add your proxy on the proxies page in the console, then pass its identifier as the proxy parameter.
secret_proxy.note: No credential-injection proxy for target sites. Only upstream-proxy credentials are stored console-side (referenced by id). Site credentials must be supplied by the client script (e.g. page.authenticate).

volume_attach.note: No storage product; browser sessions have no user disk. Not explicitly stated, derived from product shape.

volume_shared.note: No volumes/filesystems of any kind documented.
